name: Ludwigia

project_scope.scope_note: All six approved source-pool Ludwigia taxa installed as canonical learner species on 2026-10-08. L. decurrens, L. leptocarpa, L. palustris and L. peploides have independent UNRESOLVED target-zone native-range labels, not confirmed native status; initial exact-species gallery photo installed, further diagnostic macros pending.

shared_traits: Wetland or aquatic herbs with simple leaves
Flowers typically axillary, with an inferior ovary below sepals and petals
Many-seeded capsule developing from the inferior ovary
look_here_first: Check 2–3 stem nodes BEFORE the flower: Ludwigia octovalvis has alternate narrow leaves on an upright branched wetland stem; L. repens has opposite paired leaves on creeping aquatic stems (often rooting at nodes). In flower, compare flower size and count stamens: 8 versus 4. Look under petals for the inferior ovary.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Alternate (one leaf at each successive node), narrow blades; often short petioled.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Opposite/decussate (paired leaves at each node), often glossy elliptic–obovate blades.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Erect branching shoreline herb, often 0.5–2 m tall, usually taprooted/woody at base.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Aquatic, creeping to ascending shoots, roots from horizontal stem nodes, forms mats.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Williamson County material strongly 5-ridged and hairy, though FNA notes species stems may be terete or ridged.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Stem approximately cylindrical, glabrous, often reddish; rootlets can emerge at nodes.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Narrow oblanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, commonly hairy and not glossy.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: More oval/elliptic to obovate, often shiny and relatively smooth; submerged leaves may vary.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Showy bright-yellow four-petaled flowers, 23–39 mm across in local UT PRC account.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Very small yellow four-petaled flowers, about 6 mm across in local UT PRC account.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Typically 8 in 2 sets (4+4); rare five-merous flowers may have 10.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: 4 in a single whorl, one per sepal.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Conspicuously elongated inferior ovary, then long, slender 4-angled capsule; in local UT PRC account mature capsules 38–45 mm.
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Short funnel-shaped 4-angled inferior ovary; short broad bell-shaped capsule, locally 6–7.5 mm long.

comparison_matrix.ludwigia_octovalvis: Often 4–8 slender valves (8 described in local UT PRC specimens).
comparison_matrix.ludwigia_repens: Short capsule splits irregularly; sepals persist at top.

overlap_cautions: Aquatic growth form can vary with water depth; leaf arrangement and reproductive structures are stronger.
Yellow flower color alone does not identify Ludwigia.
All six source-pool Ludwigia species are now installed as canonical learner cards; source-pool counts, native-range PASS counts, and canonical concept counts must still be tracked independently.
Do not equate submerged opposite-leaved plants automatically with L. repens.
local_lookalikes: Hygrophila polysperma: submerged opposite leaves can resemble L. repens; check reproductive anatomy
All six canonical Ludwigia species are available for direct comparisons; avoid identifying sterile aquatic stems to species without reproductive confirmation.
Other Onagraceae wetland herbs: inspect inferior ovary and capsule

diagnostic_science_20261008.status: Six species now canonically installed; scientific genus-comparison review only. Preserve each species' independent native-range labels and learner approval.
look_here_first: Check opposite versus alternate leaves and rooted versus erect stems.
Count fresh petals and stamens; old petals can fall.
Check stem wings, leaf attachment and ovary position.
Measure mature fruit and pedicel; use seed/endocarp structure to confirm difficult pairs.

comparisons.diagnostic: Both opposite-leaved creepers. palustris lacks petals, sepals 1–2 mm, thin-walled fruit 1.6–5 mm; repens has four caducous petals 1.1–3 mm, sepals 1.8–5 mm, hard-walled fruit 4–10.5 mm.
comparisons.overlap: Old repens flowers may appear petal-free. Submerged habit and opposite leaves overlap.
comparisons.photos: Fresh flower and mature fruit at same scale.

comparisons.diagnostic: decurrens has sessile leaves and sharply 4-winged stem. octovalvis has 8 stamens, elongated 4-angled inferior ovary and 17–50 mm capsules.
comparisons.overlap: Both can have four yellow petals, eight stamens and upright habit. UT Austin PRC documents strongly FIVE-RIDGED stems in its Williamson County L. octovalvis subsp. octovalvis account; FNA allows terete or ridged stems across the broader species. In contrast L. decurrens has sharply FOUR-WINGED stems from decurrent sessile leaf bases. Count ridges/wings on a well-preserved internode and inspect leaf insertion, then confirm with fruit; five ridges are a locally documented character, not a universal species requirement.
comparisons.photos: Matched side and cross-lit stem internodes with scale; decurrens decurrent leaf base; octovalvis ridges arising near stipules; inferior ovaries and mature capsules.

comparisons.diagnostic: leptocarpa usually erect; seed loosely held in horseshoe-shaped endocarp segments. peploides usually creeping/floating, node-rooting, with 5-part flowers, 10 stamens and seed firmly embedded in woody endocarp.
comparisons.overlap: Emergent peploides may be ascending; habit alone unreliable.
comparisons.photos: Rooted nodes, stamen count, opened mature capsule/endocarp.

cautions: FNA gives L. octovalvis capsule dehiscence as 4–8 valves, not invariably eight.
FNA recognizes three North American L. peploides subspecies; do not equate introduced subsp. montevidensis with native subspecies.
Existing Joey octovalvis inferior-ovary frame and repens submerged-habit frame are study-only; need exact diagnostic macros.

quick_key.if: Opposite leaves; creeping mat; flower has tiny yellow petals (may be shed/absent in L. repens)
quick_key.then: Suggest Ludwigia repens — inspect mature capsule for absence of 4 green longitudinal bands before a confident split.

quick_key.if: Opposite leaves; tiny axillary flower has four GREEN SEPALS but no petals
quick_key.then: Suggest Ludwigia palustris — confirm 4 green longitudinal capsule bands, because repens can sometimes also lack petals.

quick_key.if: Opposite leaves; capsule has four dark-green longitudinal bands across its four faces
Opposite leaves; mature capsule lacks longitudinal green bands, often with tiny yellow petals present
Opposite-leaved sterile aquatic shoots only, or fruit too immature to show banding
quick_key.then: Ludwigia repens/palustris unresolved — recheck reproductive features; don't force ID

quick_key.if: Alternate narrow leaves on erect branches + usually 4 yellow petals / 8 stamens + long ribbed capsule
Alternate almost sessile leaves on erect sharply 4-winged stem (leaf bases running down ridges)
Alternate leaves on upright hairy plants + usually 5 yellow petals / 10 stamens + long hairy bumpy capsule
Alternate shiny leaves on a floating/creeping aquatic mat + usually 5 yellow petals / 10 stamens

priority: leaf arrangement: opposite pair vs alternate at nodes
growth form: erect/winged, hairy erect, creeping, floating
flower petals: absent, four or five (and stamen count 4, 8 or 10)
ovary and capsule: very short vs elongate vs winged, hairy or thin-walled
local photo confirmation, no forced native county range
study_strategy.warning: All six source-pool species have canonical learner cards. For opposite-leaved sterile mats, especially repens/palustris, verify fresh flowers or mature fruit before certainty. Keep native-range PASS/HOLD/UNRESOLVED independent of learner admission.

visual_comparison.title: Ludwigia: compare nodes, petals, and fruit bands
visual_comparison.subtitle: Photos with exact-species attribution: first identify opposite versus alternate nodes, then inspect the tiny flowers and fruit bands. A new magnified petal-less palustris flower has a verified arrow annotation.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: Opposite-leaved creeping plants: repens often has tiny yellow petals, palustris lacks them; but repens MAY lack petals. Check four dark green bands on palustris capsule vs no bands on repens.

items.label: 1A · Alternate leaves and flower
items.image_role: leaf arrangement, budding stem, flower side profile
items.caption: Study successive individual leaves on the upright stem, narrow non-glossy blades, and the elongated floral base beneath the petals. A bud is present but not a fully mature capsule.
items.creator: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata · Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 1B · Opposite leaves and aquatic branching
items.caption: Follow the reddish branches: paired leaf blades arise at stem nodes, unlike successive alternate L. octovalvis leaves. Horticultural reference, not a verified San Marcos wild plant.
items.creator: David J. Stang · Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 2A · Large flower and eight-stamen pattern
items.image_role: flower face close-up; large four-petaled flower
items.caption: Broad four yellow petals; inspect the central stamens. For flower size and stamen number use the UT PRC key; not all stamens may be resolvable in the photo.
items.creator: Juan Carlos Fonseca Mata · Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 2B · Tiny flower at the node
items.image_role: axillary small flowers, stamens and inferior ovary
items.caption: Two very small L. repens flowers with four yellow petals and four stamens, borne at an opposite-leaf node. These petals are useful when present, but may be absent or shed in some L. repens; confirm lack of capsule green bands to distinguish atypical plants from palustris.
items.creator: Kevin Thiele · Flickr via Wikimedia Commons
items.location: Photographer from Perth, Australia; subject location not confirmed

items.label: 2C · Marsh seedbox: NO petals around flower
items.image_role: true flower macro: four green sepals and no yellow petals, center of node
items.caption: A true tiny L. palustris flower (not a mature seed capsule): four green sepals frame its central reproductive disc; no yellow petals are visible. Arrow points to the sepal ring. Compare with the yellow-petaled L. repens macro—but check mature fruit bands if repens has dropped/lacks petals.
items.creator: Alex Abair · iNaturalist via Wikimedia Commons
items.provenance: Florida; exact-species iNaturalist observation, not Hays occurrence evidence

items.label: 3A · Long ribbed developing capsule
items.image_role: elongate ribbed inferior capsule with persistent green sepals
items.caption: Actual fruit close-up with long narrow ridged developing capsule below four persistent sepals. Visibly elongate, but no scale bar and not a dry, dehiscing ripe specimen.
items.creator: Alex Abair · iNaturalist via Wikimedia Commons
items.provenance: Gainesville, Florida; confirmed Wikimedia CC BY

items.label: 3B · Short fruit and rooting stem — botanical plate
items.image_role: mature fruit detail f, young fruit d, rooting prostrate stem a, seed g
items.caption: Correll & Correll 1972, fig. 562: illustration rather than photograph. Letter f shows mature fruit; d young fruit; e fruit section; g seed; a creeping rooted stem. Not a substitute for an actual rooted-node macro photo.
items.creator: Correll & Correll / EPA 1972; R. K. Godfrey illustration; Internet Archive scan
items.license: Public domain in USA per Wikimedia Commons file record
items.provenance: Scientific line drawing, no photographic specimen or site

items.label: 4 · Wing-leaved primrose-willow
items.image_role: four yellow petals and lanceolate foliage; winged stem diagnostic not shown clearly
items.caption: Four-petaled flower of L. decurrens. The strongest field split from L. octovalvis is a sharply four-winged stem and sessile leaf base running down the stem; this flower photograph does not prove those features.
items.creator: Sesamehoneytart · Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 5 · Hairy primrose-willow
items.image_role: five-petaled yellow flower and leafy upright stem
items.caption: Identified L. leptocarpa flower and leafy stems from Costa Rica. Inspect five petals here; the diagnostic hairy, long, bumpy capsules and leaf hairs still need sharper macro evidence.
items.creator: Franz Xaver · Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 6 · Petal-less marsh seedbox
items.image_role: opposite leaves and small green four-sepaled axillary fruiting structures
items.caption: Opposite leaves along red creeping stem; tiny green sepals and young fruits at nodes, rather than showy yellow petals. This is the dangerous vegetative look-alike of L. repens; capsule green striping and lack of petals improve separation.
items.creator: Alex Abair · iNaturalist via Wikimedia Commons

items.label: 7 · Floating primrose-willow
items.image_role: floating creeping stems, alternate shiny leaves and five-petaled flower
items.caption: Subspecies peploides from California: shiny alternate leaves, floating stems, and five broad yellow petals. The petiole, calyx, capsule and bracteoles require closer photos before separating subspecies.
items.creator: Eugene Zelenko · Wikimedia Commons

visual_comparison.overlay_note: L. palustris 278592882 shows an actual four-sepal petal-less flower (not a mature fruit); repens Kevin Thiele shows yellow petals. source_pool_species_comparison.name: Ludwigia decurrens
source_pool_species_comparison.look_here_first: Run fingers/eyes down stem: sharply four-angled and winged from sessile decurrent leaf bases.
source_pool_species_comparison.comparison: Against upright L. octovalvis: winged 4-angled stem + sessile blade base, not merely local octovalvis longitudinal ridges; 4 yellow petals and usually 8 stamens overlap.

source_pool_species_comparison.name: Ludwigia leptocarpa
source_pool_species_comparison.look_here_first: Erect or ascending often hairy stems, lanceolate alternate leaves, 5 yellow petals and usually 10 stamens.
source_pool_species_comparison.comparison: Against L. octovalvis: typically 5-merous rather than 4-merous; thin-walled, long-hairy capsule with seed impressions (bumps) instead of smoother more woody pod. Against peploides: generally erect, hairy and with long narrow capsule, not low floating glossy mat.

source_pool_species_comparison.native_range_status: UNRESOLVED — do not count target-zone native without range review

source_pool_species_comparison.name: Ludwigia palustris
source_pool_species_comparison.look_here_first: Opposite leaves on creeping wet-mud plant; tiny axillary flowers with sepals but NO yellow petals.
source_pool_species_comparison.comparison: Against L. repens: normally apetalous vs four tiny yellow petals, green longitudinal capsule bands often visible in L. palustris vs absent in L. repens. Sterile shoots often cannot be safely separated.
source_pool_species_comparison.photo_status: licensed leaf/fruit close-up anchor; close green capsule stripes reference only; first learner photo now installed locally

source_pool_species_comparison.name: Ludwigia peploides
source_pool_species_comparison.look_here_first: Floating or creeping mat with ALTERNATE shiny broadly elliptic leaves and usually 5 showy yellow petals (10 stamens).
source_pool_species_comparison.comparison: Against L. repens/palustris: alternate leaves, larger showy flowers with 10 stamens. Against L. leptocarpa: creeping/floating with glossy blades; fruit generally shorter and thick-walled; subspecies distinction needs mature reproductive material.

octovalvis_local_stem_diagnostic_2026100.regional_evidence: UT Austin Plant Resources Center, Vascular Plants of Williamson County: stems strongly 5-ridged, under 9 mm diameter; two ridges descend from stipules on the internode.
octovalvis_local_stem_diagnostic_2026100.species_wide_caution: FNA keys L. octovalvis more broadly with stems that can be terete or ridged; the five-ridge local account must not become a universal exclusion character.
octovalvis_local_stem_diagnostic_2026100.contrast: L. decurrens has sharply 4-winged stems and sessile decurrent leaf bases; L. octovalvis leaves are subsessile and stems may be ridged rather than winged.
look_here_first: Photograph and examine a mature stem internode and leaf insertion in profile.
Distinguish four thin wings formed by decurrent leaf bases from local five longitudinal ridges, including stipular ridges.
Confirm fresh flower and mature capsule; do not force identification from stem ridges alone.
diagnostic_photo_roles: Exact-species L. octovalvis subsp. octovalvis stem with five ridges visible, scale and stipules in frame.
Matched exact-species L. decurrens stem with four sharp wings and decurrent leaf bases.
Scaled stem transverse sections and mature capsule comparison; prefer existing user/Joey project media before sourcing.
octovalvis_local_stem_diagnostic_2026100.review_level: Scientific morphology clarification; no changes to range or installation.

repens_palustris_comparison.look_here_first: Both species have opposite leaf pairs on creeping wetland stems; vegetative habit alone is NOT definitive. Find a small axillary flower and mature fruit.
repens_palustris_comparison.flower: L. palustris usually lacks petals (four green sepals remain). L. repens usually bears four tiny yellow petals, but petals are caducous and some plants may be naturally apetalous.
repens_palustris_comparison.reproductive_tie_breaker: Look for four longitudinal dark-green bands on the four sides of the L. palustris ovary/capsule; absent from L. repens. This is better than absent petals alone.
repens_palustris_comparison.fruit_size: L. palustris typically around 2–5 mm long, L. repens often 4–10 mm (Flora of North America); dimensions overlap and should not be used alone.
repens_palustris_comparison.photo_state: Bright, exact-species petal-less flower macro of palustris with checked arrow + flowering repens macro both live. Matched ripe capsules with visible green banding and ruler NOT yet acquired.
